title: Legendre/parity coordinate predicates show no k-dependence
question: For random prime-order curves E/F_p and generator P, the predicates chi(x([k]P)), chi(y([k]P)), parity of x([k]P) are statistically independent of k mod m for small m and have no detectable autocorrelation in k.
rationale: Registered by PI from sealed round-1 submissions before cross-agent synthesis or review.
claims: For random prime-order curves E/F_p and generator P, the predicates chi(x([k]P)), chi(y([k]P)), parity of x([k]P) are statistically independent of k mod m for small m and have no detectable autocorrelation in k.
next_action: Resolve the spectral anomaly via HYP-242da418 before any conclusion.
notes: Origin: A6/E1 (RUN-b0ccd1bd); empirical only, 2 curves at p ~ 10^4, no multiple-testing correction. Converse direction of known hard-core-bit results. | ECDLP-7 E-B (120 curves x 2 seeds, p in [1e3,1e5]): 0 Bonferroni rejections for dependence on k mod m; but pre-registered KS of p-values failed for DFT-max/lag-1 tests of chi(x), chi(y) (flatter spectrum than random). Original claim of "no detectable autocorrelation" is thus NOT supported as stated; the anomaly is a spectral-law deviation, not shown to be a k-leak. See HYP-242da418.
